transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

It is unlikely that your hob is about to break. Induction hobs work by creating a magnetic field in the pan, which can cause heavy or multi-layered pots (like large stockpots) to vibrate and produce a humming or buzzing noise at high power; this is normal behaviour for induction technology. To confirm this is just normal operation and not an issue with the cookware itself, please check two things: first, does the noise stop if you lower the power setting from 'high'? Second, can you stick a magnet to the base of that stockpot? If it has a flat magnetic base and the noise reduces at lower settings, it is probably just normal induction hum.

Yes, it's much quieter at 6 and below. I haven't tried a magnet on the pot yet, but I can do that. The base is a sandwich base, maybe slightly smaller than the ring, if that matters.

That suggests it is normal behaviour. Induction hobs naturally hum or buzz at high power because the magnetic field causes the metal in the pan to vibrate; this is especially common with heavy stockpots and reduces significantly when you lower the heat. Regarding your pot: if the base is slightly smaller than the heating ring, it may increase the noise slightly as the magnetic field has less surface area to grip, but this does not damage the hob. As long as the pan sits flat and stable, there is no risk of failure. You do not need to test with a magnet; the fact that it works on induction and quiets down at lower settings is all the confirmation needed.
